To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alternative promoters are used for the transcription of adjacent maize chloroplast polystromic transcription units, and that the resulting overlapping transcripts are developmentally regulated.

transcription initiation at multiple promoters within and between transcription units contributes to the generation and regulation of the complex pattern of overlapping RNAs that accumulate from the adjacent psbE-psbf-psbL- ORF40 and ORf31-petE-pORF42 transcription units.
the maize chloroplast psbE-psbf-psbL and ORF31-psbE-ORF40 transcription units are co-transcribed and that the petE-ORF31 transcription unit is regulated by light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization and expression of the maize chloroplast genome.
the organization of transcription units and the generation of overlapping RNA molecules in the maize chloroplast genome.
the regulation of gene expression within chloroplast polycitronic transcription units.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

alternative promoters are used for transcription initiation in maize chloroplast polychistronic transcription units, and the use of alternative promoters contributes to overlapping transcript patterns for both gene clusters.
the overlapping transcripts of these transcription units result from the use of alternative promoters.
the overlapping transcripts in the region are a result of alternative transcription initiation sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maize chloroplast genome has evolved a complex transcriptional organization that is not only capable of generating multiple transcripts, but also of generating transcript ratios that vary with developmental stage.
alternative promoters are used for the transcription of genes within maize chloro-plast polycistronic transcripts.
the overlapping transcripts for the two gene cluster and the divergently transcribed genes are generated in large part by transcription initiation from alternative promoters.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transcription units for chloroplast genes are more complex than previously thought, and that alternative transcription initiation is a common mechanism for the generation of overlapping transcripts.
alternative promoters contribute to the generation of the diverse transcript populations for these two gene clusters and that promoter usage contributes to the regulation of gene expression.
alternative transcriptional start sites can be used to generate overlapping RNAs in a developmentally regulated manner.
